schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: db_domain's socket client, published as a tool nested in the device: connect, read, write, update, query, delete, create_owned_table, owner_of and scratch over the one owner-gated store. Every caller in the repo talks to the database through this module and nothing else of db_domain's.
why: RULE 1 agreed detail (2) (Akien, 2026-10-01): "there should still be a public interface everyone uses, so we can change things about the db underneath." Measured before the build: 48 imports from 46 files reached into db_domain's own store.py, so any change to the device's insides could break any of them. The client talks straight to the db over its socket — no bus hop — because graph-tree traffic is too heavy to pay a bus round trip per row.
entry: GRAFTED by git mv from cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py, ticket 4cbf6e28126e, 2026-10-01. The module's bytes moved unchanged; every importer's dotted path was rewritten, its alias and comment kept.
invoke: `from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client import store` (and `from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store import OwnershipError`). Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py` (exit 0 = green). Provisioning (the OS-named LOGIN CREATEDB role) stays db_domain's, in its charter's state.
state_and_history: A TOOL HOLDS NO STATE OF ITS OWN (Law 6): the tables it reads and writes are owned by the caller that created them, gated by the owner CHECK in the store. Its design history rides db_domain's history.json under ticket 4cbf6e28126e.
proof: proofs/test_client.py — three teeth, one per falsifier clause of 4cbf6e28126e: nothing reaches into db_domain (encapsulation_breaches carries no row targeting it); the old door is gone (no importer of cairn.devices.db_domain.store, the file gone, no charter invoke naming it); the client is published (this charter's two fields, and the module exposes its surface). The names resolve late, so a hollow revert reds tooth by tooth.
gates: Import gate — encapsulation_holds in build_inspector (RULE 1, ticket 56d1aff4455e) admits a reach into db_domain only through this tool, because this charter says published_by_device and names its one module. Seal: the tester seals proofs/test_client.py into validations/ beside it.
falsifier: Red if any import outside db_domain lands on db_domain code other than cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store, if anything still imports cairn.devices.db_domain.store, or if this charter stops declaring published_by_device and exactly its one module.
learns: It does not; it is a connection client, deliberately dumb physics — the fixed floor the graph trees learn on.
how_it_learns: It does not; it is a connection client, deliberately dumb physics — the fixed floor the graph trees learn on.
traces_to: RULE 1 (encapsulation — a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes)
Law 6 (one owner per table; the owner CHECK lives in this module)
Law 4 (the owner gate is a schema CHECK, not a convention)
owner: None of its own — a tool has users (Law 6): every component that talks to the database. Its code is held by db_domain, which publishes it; CC gates writes to that code and its proofs.
